<thought>To meet the requirement of a single‑step synthesis from commercially available chemicals, the most straightforward disconnection is a McMurry coupling of two equivalents of p‑anisaldehyde (4‑methoxybenzaldehyde). This reaction breaks the aldehyde C=O bonds and forms the central C=C bond of the target 4,4′‑dimethoxystilbene. p‑Anisaldehyde is inexpensive and readily purchasable, and the total cost of the starting material is well below $150. The retrosynthesis tree therefore consists of one reaction node (McMurry coupling) with a single leaf node representing p‑anisaldehyde (used twice). The JSON below follows the required schema.</thought>
